scope: G4c preregistration. What the general-dimension reading of the G4b mechanism predicts, written down BEFORE any measurement outside d = 2 was run. Theory-track; nothing frozen in the prereg sense, but this file is committed ahead of the harness so that a post-hoc fit is not available as an option.

state_of_evidence_when_written.d=1: measured (G4b control): extra flexes at every (n, R) tested; never rigid
state_of_evidence_when_written.d=2: measured (G4b): R = 3 gives nullity 9 = gauge 3 + 6 extra, constant over n = 6..34; R >= 4 reaches nullity = gauge 3; R = 2 NOT tested

mechanism.statement: The centered profile map x -> Phi~(x) sends R^d into the (R-1)-dimensional mean-zero subspace of R^R. Its image is a d-dimensional surface. Everything follows from the sign of (R-1) - d.

under_observed.mechanism: the map is a submersion with fibres of dimension d - R + 1; a target slides along its fibre without changing Phi~ at all
under_observed.signature: nullity grows linearly in n, with slope d - R + 1

saturated.mechanism: the surface fills its ambient space, so D is merely the distance matrix of n points in R^d and the freedom is realizable by moving the observers
saturated.signature: nullity constant in n, above the gauge

curved.mechanism: the surface is a genuinely curved d-surface in a >= (d+1)-dimensional ambient; curvature rigidifies
curved.signature: nullity == gauge == d(d+1)/2 once n is large enough

mechanism.why_d_equals_1_is_exempt_from_the_curved: |x - p| is piecewise linear in one dimension, so the profile 'surface' is a polyline of exactly zero curvature and the rigidifying mechanism is absent at every R. This exemption is specific to d = 1 and is not expected to recur at d >= 2.
mechanism.calibration: This reading reproduces the measured d = 2 numbers: R = 3 is the saturated regime (R - 1 == d) and R >= 4 is the curved regime, which is exactly where the measured threshold sits.

predictions.claim: nullity grows linearly in n with slope 1 (fibre dimension d - R + 1 = 1)
predictions.falsified_if: nullity is constant in n, or the fitted slope is not 1
predictions.basis: pure dimension count of a submersion; no free parameter

predictions.claim: nullity == 18 and extra flexes == 12, constant in n
predictions.falsified_if: nullity is not 18, or varies with n
predictions.basis: counting heuristic calibrated on a SINGLE measured point (nullity 9 at d = 2, R = 3 = 2*3 + 3). The regime assignment is strong; the specific number is the weakest prediction in this file and is the one most worth being wrong.

predictions.falsified_if: extra flexes remain positive at every n tested
predictions.basis: the same curvature argument that already produced the measured R >= 4 threshold at d = 2

predictions.claim: the observed threshold exceeds the naive constraint-counting bound n >= 9
predictions.basis: the bound was not tight at d = 2 (7 predicted, 11 measured), so tightness at d = 3 would be a surprise

predictions.claim: nullity grows linearly in n with slope 1 (fibre dimension d - R + 1 = 1)
predictions.basis: a retro-check in the ALREADY understood dimension. The regime law implies an under-observed regime at d = 2 too, at R = 2, which G4b never tested. If this fails the law is wrong before d = 3 is reached.

what_this_does_not_predict: global uniqueness -- every prediction here is about infinitesimal rigidity, i.e. the rank of one Jacobian
anything about noisy or delta-quantized D; the model is exact
anything about D harvested through the instrument from a measured causal set
the d >= 4 case, which the mechanism covers but which is not measured here
